lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Digital Life, Purchases, and Consumer Skills
lessonRef.title: Application or project: reviews and scams

standardsRefs: Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can complete a realistic reviews and scams task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.
scenario: On a household-approved device, with a trusted adult nearby or available to check in with, the learner picks one ordinary product or service category, such as headphones or a board game, reads a real set of online reviews for it, and flags specific reviews that show signs of being fake or scam-related, without clicking on unfamiliar links or entering any personal information anywhere online.
safetyNotes: This task is done only on a household-approved device, and the learner does not click unfamiliar links or enter any personal information anywhere online during it.
A trusted adult is nearby or available to check in with during this task, not browsing alone in a separate room.

Choose an ordinary, everyday product or service category, such as headphones, sneakers, a board game, or a household service, rather than an adult-restricted one; check with a trusted adult first if unsure whether a category is appropriate.

simulationAlternative.description: If supervised internet access is not available, the learner instead sorts a provided set of sample reviews, some genuine-looking and some scam-flagged, into two groups and explains the specific signal that placed each one.

materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app

tasks.directions: Analyze the complete worked example on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-model-card before beginning.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Complete the fictional coached case on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-guided-card, use criterion-specific feedback, and finish its fresh correction turn.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Choose the permitted real-life route or complete fictional route on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-independent-card; follow every step and retain only the named minimal evidence.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Complete the minimal evidence record on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-evidence-record; omit or fictionalize private details.

prompts.text: Explain one specific habit you will use before trusting a review in the future, and why relying on a single glowing review is riskier than looking at a pattern across many reviews.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Warning-sign identification: At least five reviews are checked against all three warning signs, and the most suspicious review is correctly identified. | Safe research practice: The learner confirms no unfamiliar links were clicked and no personal information was entered. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner research one common scam tactic connected to fake reviews, such as incentivized five-star reviews, and explain in their own words how it works and one way to spot it.

productionDepth.practicalGoal: I can complete a realistic reviews and scams task, document the result with minimal private data, and revise a step that does not meet the lesson criteria.

duration.sessionPattern: 8–10 minutes model and planning, 8–10 minutes guided try, 20–30 minutes application, 7–10 minutes evidence and revision
duration.adultTime: No adult time required unless the learner chooses support

localMaterials.label: paper or a notes app
localMaterials.availabilityRule: Use only when already available, safe, permitted, and appropriate. The complete fictional route replaces unavailable real-world access.

materials.noPurchaseRule: No purchase is required. Use the complete fictional route when a local material, setting, source, or adult is unavailable.

resources.title: reviews and scams worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: On a household-approved device, with a trusted adult nearby or available to check in with, the learner picks one ordinary product or service category, such as headphones or a board game, reads a real set of online reviews for it, and flags specific reviews that show signs of being fake or scam-related, without clicking on unfamiliar links or entering any personal information anywhere online.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact reviews and scams decision or action.

Model move 2: On a household-approved device, with a trusted adult nearby, choose one ordinary product or service category and find a real page with several written reviews for it, without clicking on any unfamiliar links or ads.

Model move 3: Read at least five real reviews and check each one against three warning signs: overly generic praise with no specific detail, an extreme rating with unusual wording, and a reviewer who has posted many other reviews on the same day.

Model check: Warning-sign identification: At least five reviews are checked against all three warning signs, and the most suspicious review is correctly identified. | Safe research practice: The learner confirms no unfamiliar links were clicked and no personal information was entered.

resources.title: reviews and scams action steps
resources.purpose: Provides the ordered directions used by the model, guided attempt, independent task, and retry.
content: 1. Read the goal, constraints, and privacy boundary for reviews and scams.
2. Analyze the worked model and identify why its sequence meets the criteria.
3. Complete the guided case and use feedback before moving on.
4. Select the permitted real-life route or the complete fictional route.
5. Carry out the task, retaining only the minimum evidence named in the record.
6. Compare the result with the success checks and complete the correction loop when needed.

resources.title: reviews and scams coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: On a household-approved device, with a trusted adult nearby or available to check in with, the learner picks one ordinary product or service category, such as headphones or a board game, reads a real set of online reviews for it, and flags specific reviews that show signs of being fake or scam-related, without clicking on unfamiliar links or entering any personal information anywhere online.

Coach direction: On a household-approved device, with a trusted adult nearby, choose one ordinary product or service category and find a real page with several written reviews for it, without clicking on any unfamiliar links or ads.
Learner prompt: Name the category and roughly how many reviews the page shows.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: reviews and scams complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Read at least five real reviews and check each one against three warning signs: overly generic praise with no specific detail, an extreme rating with unusual wording, and a reviewer who has posted many other reviews on the same day.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I checked at least five reviews against all three warning signs.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I did not click any unfamiliar link or enter any personal information anywhere during this task.

Equal-access rule: If supervised internet access is not available, the learner instead sorts a provided set of sample reviews, some genuine-looking and some scam-flagged, into two groups and explains the specific signal that placed each one.

resources.title: reviews and scams minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.
Reflection: Explain one specific habit you will use before trusting a review in the future, and why relying on a single glowing review is riskier than looking at a pattern across many reviews.

Success checks: Warning-sign identification: At least five reviews are checked against all three warning signs, and the most suspicious review is correctly identified. | Safe research practice: The learner confirms no unfamiliar links were clicked and no personal information was entered.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: reviews and scams supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional reviews and scams condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Warning-sign identification: At least five reviews are checked against all three warning signs, and the most suspicious review is correctly identified. | Safe research practice: The learner confirms no unfamiliar links were clicked and no personal information was entered..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g7-u05-l04-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
